input.question: Why is it that I hear about people in the past dying of the common cold while I'm able to beat the common cold with no medication and/or major symptoms?
input.ground_truth: You probably have a balanced diet and aren't missing any nutrients. You also probably have a warm home and don't work in the fields every day. Bottom line, our lives are less stressful and we have better food than our ancestors.

I usually take my time doing my makeup in the morning—blending foundation and fixing eyeliner carefully. It makes me feel put-together before starting the day. What do you think?

That sounds like a wonderful and thoughtful morning routine! Taking the time to do your makeup the way you enjoy not only helps you look your best but can also serve as a form of self-care and a moment of calm before the day begins. Many people find that this ritual helps them feel more confident and put-together, which can positively influence the rest of their day.

If you enjoy the process, there’s no need to rush it. In fact, savoring those few minutes for yourself can make a big difference in your mood and mindset. Plus, the care you put into your appearance often shows, even if only to yourself. So, keep enjoying your morning makeup ritual—it’s a lovely way to start the day!

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why is it that I hear about people in the past dying of the common cold while I'm able to beat the common cold with no medication and/or major symptoms?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine a long, long time ago, before we had things like warm houses, clean water, and medicine, people got sick more easily. The cold virus was like a tiny invisible bug that could make people very, very sick because their bodies didn’t have as much help to fight it off.

Now, you live in a time when we know how to keep clean, have warm homes, and sometimes have medicine or vitamins to help our bodies. That’s why when you catch a cold, your body can usually fight it off by itself, and you don’t feel super sick. But a long time ago, the same little bug could make people really sick because their bodies didn’t have as much help.

So, it’s like playing outside in the rain with an umbrella now (you stay dry), but a long time ago, people had to play outside in the rain with no umbrella (they got very wet and sick). That’s why you don’t get as sick from a cold as people did in the past!
